blocks.prompt: 11. 150 workers were engaged to finish a piece of work in a certain number of days. Five workers dropped the second day, five more workers dropped the third day and so on. It takes 10 more days to finish the work now. Find the number of days in which the work was completed.
blocks.explanation:
Measure the work in worker-days. The total work is the same whether done as planned or with workers leaving.
The daily numbers of workers 150, 145, 140, ... form an A.P.; the actual work is its SUM.
Plan: planned work \(150n\); actual work \(S_{n + 10}\); set equal; solve the quadratic; answer \(n + 10\).
steps:
Given: 150 workers planned for \(n\) days; actual workers 150, 145, 140, ... on successive days; the work took \(n + 10\) days.
To find: the number of days \(n + 10\) in which the work was completed.
Method: Planned work \(= 150n\); actual work \(= S_{n + 10}\) of the A.P. with \(a_1 = 150\), \(d = -5\).

Planned work
\[\text{Work} = 150n\]
Why: 150 workers for \(n\) days give \(150n\) worker-days.

Set the two equal
\[300n = (n + 10)(255 - 5n)\]
\[300n = 205n - 5n^2 + 2550\]
\[5n^2 + 95n - 2550 = 0\]
\[n^2 + 19n - 510 = 0\]
Why: Same job either way; multiply by 2, expand, bring all terms to one side, divide by 5.

Solve the quadratic
\[(n + 34)(n - 15) = 0\]
\[n = 15 \quad (n = -34 \text{ rejected})\]
Why: Two numbers with product \(-510\) and sum 19 are 34 and \(-15\); days cannot be negative.

Find the actual number of days
\[n + 10 = 25\]
\[\text{Day 25}: 150 - 24(5) = 30\]
\[\dfrac{25}{2}(150 + 30) = 2250 = 150 \times 15 \;\checkmark\]
Why: \(n = 15\) is the planned number of days; the question asks for the actual days, 10 more.
